summary.text: Jim Risch is the incumbent Republican U.S. Senator from Idaho, first elected in 2008 and now serving his third term. A lawyer and rancher by background, he spent decades in Idaho politics as a county prosecutor, state senator, lieutenant governor and, briefly, governor before joining the Senate. According to his Senate website, he chairs the Foreign Relations Committee and also serves on the Energy and Natural Resources, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, Intelligence and Ethics committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee from 1961 to 1963 before moving to the University of Idaho.
Received a bachelor's degree in forestry (1965) and a law degree (1968) from the University of Idaho, where he served on the Law Review.

Won election as Ada County Prosecuting Attorney in 1970, serving two terms. During that time he taught criminal justice classes at Boise State and served as president of the state prosecuting attorneys' association.

Was first elected to the Idaho Senate in 1974 and served there for many years, where his Republican colleagues chose him as Majority Leader and President Pro Tempore. He lost a 1988 re-election bid and returned to the chamber in 1995 by appointment.
Was twice elected Idaho's Lieutenant Governor, first in 2002 and again in 2006.

Became Idaho's 31st Governor on May 26, 2006, when Gov. Dirk Kempthorne resigned to become U.S. Secretary of the Interior, and served the remaining months of the term. According to his Senate website, his governorship included property tax reform that cut property taxes by 20% and $100 million in additional funding for public schools.
Was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2008, defeating former U.S. Rep. Larry LaRocco, and took office in January 2009. He was re-elected in 2014 and 2020.
In the Senate, he serves as Chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee and sits on the Energy and Natural Resources, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, Intelligence, and Ethics committees.

Outside public service, he is a rancher, small business owner, and former senior partner in the Risch Goss Insinger Gustavel law firm. According to his Senate website, he and his wife, Vicki, live on a ranch outside Boise and have three sons and nine grandchildren.
